Last week I went on a trip to Kyoto with a friend. We planned to take the 7 a.m. shinkansen, but the train was two hours late because of snow. (1) So we arrived in Kyoto at about twelve.
In Kyoto we saw old temples and shrines. At night we stayed at a ryokan. The staff were very kind and (2) gave us a map of the town.
On the last day, I went to buy souvenirs for my family. The shop had many things like sweets and chopsticks, so I (3) couldn't decide easily. I bought my mother some pretty chopsticks. I plan to give them to her when I go home next week. I'll be happy (4) if she likes them.

reading.en:
To Mr. Tanaka
The department manager called. The shinkansen from Osaka has stopped because of an accident, so he will not be back at the office until the evening. He said he would like today's 3 o'clock meeting to be moved to 10 a.m. tomorrow. Please change the meeting room booking. I have already told the people at the meeting by email.
Yamashita, October 21, 1 p.m.

{二日目|ふつかめ}、{札幌|さっぽろ}から{小樽|おたる}という{町|まち}へ{電車|でんしゃ}で{行|い}くことにしました。しかし、{駅|えき}に{着|つ}くと、{大雪|おおゆき}のため、{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まっていました。{駅|えき}のアナウンスは{速|はや}くて、{私|わたし}にはよくわかりませんでした。どうしたらいいかわからなくて{困|こま}っていると、{隣|となり}にいたおばあさんが「{電車|でんしゃ}は{一時間|いちじかん}ぐらいで{動|うご}くそうですよ。{待|ま}つ{間|あいだ}、あそこの{喫茶店|きっさてん}で{温|あたた}かいものでも{飲|の}みましょう」と{言|い}ってくれました。
{喫茶店|きっさてん}で、おばあさんは{小樽|おたる}のおすすめの{店|みせ}を{教|おし}えてくれました。{私|わたし}が{国|くに}の{家族|かぞく}にお{土産|みやげ}を{買|か}いたいと{言|い}うと、ガラスの{店|みせ}がいいと{言|い}って、{地図|ちず}もかいてくれました。

reading.en:
Last winter I went to Hokkaido alone. It was my first solo trip since coming to Japan.
On the second day, I decided to go by train from Sapporo to a town called Otaru. But when I got to the station, the trains had stopped because of heavy snow. The station announcement was fast and I couldn't understand it well. While I was at a loss, an old woman next to me said, "I hear the trains will move in about an hour. While we wait, let's have something warm to drink at that cafe."
At the cafe, she told me about good shops in Otaru. When I said I wanted to buy souvenirs for my family back home, she said a glass shop would be good and even drew me a map.
In the end, the train left an hour and a half later than planned. In Otaru I went to the shop she told me about and bought my mother a glass cup. The delay was hard, but thanks to it, I got the best memory of my trip.

listening.question: {何|なん}と{言|い}いますか。
options: {大阪|おおさか}へ{行|い}ったことがありますか。
{大阪|おおさか}{行|い}きの{電車|でんしゃ}が{来|き}ましたよ。
{大阪|おおさか}{行|い}きの{電車|でんしゃ}は{何番線|なんばんせん}ですか。
listening.en: You want to go to Osaka but don't know which platform the train leaves from. What do you say to a station worker?
listening.why: You ask which platform the Osaka train uses.

listening.setup: {旅行|りょこう}から{帰|かえ}りました。{会社|かいしゃ}の{人|ひと}にお{土産|みやげ}をあげます。{何|なん}と{言|い}いますか。
listening.question: {何|なん}と{言|い}いますか。
options: これ、{旅行|りょこう}のお{土産|みやげ}です。どうぞ。
これ、お{土産|みやげ}をくださいませんか。
listening.en: You are back from a trip and give a souvenir to a coworker. What do you say?
listening.why: You are giving, so you say 'This is a souvenir from my trip. Please.'

listening.setup: {電車|でんしゃ}がこんでいます。{次|つぎ}の{駅|えき}で{降|お}りたいですが、ドアの{前|まえ}に{人|ひと}がたくさんいます。{何|なん}と{言|い}いますか。
listening.question: {何|なん}と{言|い}いますか。
options: すみません、{乗|の}ります。
すみません、{降|お}ります。
すみません、{降|お}りてください。
listening.en: The train is crowded. You want to get off at the next station, but many people are in front of the door. What do you say?
listening.why: '{降|お}ります' tells people you are getting off.

listening.setup: {友|とも}だちがこれから{旅行|りょこう}に{出|で}かけます。{何|なん}と{言|い}いますか。
listening.question: {何|なん}と{言|い}いますか。
options: {気|き}をつけて{行|い}ってらっしゃい。
{気|き}をつけて{行|い}ってきます。
お{帰|かえ}りなさい。{楽|たの}しかった？
listening.en: Your friend is leaving for a trip now. What do you say?
listening.why: {行|い}ってらっしゃい is said to someone who is leaving; {行|い}ってきます is said by the person leaving.

lines.jp: すみません、この{席|せき}、{空|あ}いていますか。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: はい、どういたしまして。
listening.en: M: Excuse me, is this seat free?
listening.why: 'Yes, go ahead' answers a question about a free seat.

lines.jp: {電車|でんしゃ}、なかなか{来|き}ませんね。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: ええ、{事故|じこ}があったそうですよ。
ええ、{早|はや}く{着|つ}きましたね。
いいえ、{遅|おく}れてすみません。
listening.en: F: The train just isn't coming, is it?
listening.why: Agreeing and giving the reason (an accident) fits.

lines.jp: お{部屋|へや}は{和室|わしつ}と{洋室|ようしつ}、どちらがよろしいですか。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: {和室|わしつ}をお{願|ねが}いします。
listening.en: M: Would you like a Japanese-style room or a Western-style room?
listening.why: The guest chooses one of the two rooms.

lines.jp: {北海道|ほっかいどう}のお{土産|みやげ}です。{皆|みな}さんでどうぞ。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: わあ、ありがとうございます。
どうぞ、{召|め}し{上|あ}がってください。
listening.en: F: It's a souvenir from Hokkaido. Please share it, everyone.
listening.why: You thank someone who gives you a souvenir.

lines.jp: {明日|あした}、{何時|なんじ}の{新幹線|しんかんせん}に{乗|の}るの？

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: {東京|とうきょう}から{乗|の}るよ。
{二時間|にじかん}ぐらいかかるよ。
{九時|くじ}のに{乗|の}るつもり。
listening.en: M: What time is the shinkansen you're taking tomorrow?
listening.why: The question asks what time, so 'the nine o'clock one' answers it.

lines.jp: すみません、チェックインは{何時|なんじ}からできますか。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: {十一時|じゅういちじ}までにお{願|ねが}いします。
{三時|さんじ}からでございます。
{一泊|いっぱく}でございます。
listening.en: F: Excuse me, from what time can I check in?
listening.why: It asks from what time, so 'from three o'clock' is the answer.

lines.jp: {旅行|りょこう}、{楽|たの}しんできてね。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: うん、{楽|たの}しかったよ。
うん、ありがとう。お{土産|みやげ}{買|か}ってくるね。
うん、{楽|たの}しんでいってね。
listening.en: M: Enjoy your trip.
listening.why: The trip hasn't happened yet, so you thank him and promise a souvenir.

lines.jp: {切符|きっぷ}、なくさないようにね。

listening.question: {何|なん}と{答|こた}えますか。
options: うん、なくしてもいいよ。
うん、ちゃんとかばんに{入|い}れたよ。
listening.en: F: Make sure you don't lose your ticket.
listening.why: Saying you put it safely in your bag answers the warning.
